title: A generalization of the Dirichlet approximation theorem for affine actions on the real line
comment: This is a revised version of a published article
summary: We study quantitative density of orbits of the free semigroup $Γ$ generated by two maps of $(0,\infty)$. For the Möbius pair $x\mapsto 1/x$, $x\mapsto x+1$ we show that every orbit is $O(n^{-1})$-dense in $[0,\infty)$, that every irrational number $u$ is approached at a rate governed by the continued fraction of $u$ (at least $n^{-2}$, exponential when $u$ has bounded partial quotients, and $\exp(-cn/\log n)$ for almost every $u$), and that for rational $u$ and rational starting points the rate $n^{-1}$ is optimal. For the affine pair $T_0(x)=x/a$, $T_1(x)=bx+1$ with $a,b>1$, which was studied by Bergelson, Misiurewicz and Senti, we prove that for every $x>0$ and $u\ge 0$ there are infinitely many $γ\inΓ$ with \[ |γ(x)-u|<C\,λ^{-|γ|},\qquad λ=\exp\!\Big(\frac{\log a\,\log\frac{a}{a-1}}{\log\frac{a^2b}{a-1}}\Big)>1, \] where $|γ|$ is the word length of $γ$ and $C$ is independent of $γ$. This exponential rate holds whether or not $\log_a b$ is rational, and the exponential order cannot be improved for almost every $u$. We also give a corrected version of the Kronecker-type estimate $|γ(x)-u|<(u+1)(t^{1/|γ|}-1)$. Finally, we discuss the approximation of real numbers by ratios of primes and by ratios of logarithms of primes, updated in light of recent results on gaps between primes.

title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over sextic fields
comment: 36 pages. This paper will become part of a paper covering degrees 6 to 9 (degree 10 will be a separate paper) in the future, see the AI disclosure and future work in the paper
summary: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $6$. Apart from the $44$ groups that occur infinitely often, which were determined by Derickx and Sutherland, exactly four groups occur: $\mathbb{Z}/25\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$. The first three were known to occur, while the group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is new. We also show that, up to isomorphism, each of the groups $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is the torsion group of a single elliptic curve over a single sextic field. The methods build on those developed by Derickx and Najman for quartic fields and by the author for quintic fields. Among the new ingredients are a formal immersion criterion at the prime $2$ which uses the Cartier operator, and arguments with several diamond operators and with cuspidal divisor classes on quotients of modular curves.

title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
summary: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some instances of modularity in this situation. Our main result is that $ρ$ is modular if it is non-split at every place above $p$ where it is reducible, by combining Zhang's pro-modularity theorem with a classicality criterion based on Emerton's ordinary parts. Together with a theorem of Zhao on local indecomposability, this gives the modularity of the $λ$-adic representations attached to abelian varieties of $\GL_2$-type in the mixed case, and, using a result of Snowden, of potentially modular representations of parallel weight two under a mild additional condition. It also gives the modularity of representations whose local type at every place above $p$ is of discrete series type, and, through a member of the compatible system with interchanged Hodge-Tate weights, of potentially modular representations of weight $(2,k)$ over real quadratic fields with Steinberg type at one place above $p$, under conditions on that member.

title: Ramanujan-type congruences for the smallest parts function
summary:
In a famous paper of Andrews, he defined and studied the smallest parts function $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. He showed that it satisfies the three Ramanujan-type congruences:
  \[ \operatorname{spt}(5n+4)\equiv0\pmod5,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(7n+5)\equiv0\pmod7,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(13n+6)\equiv0\pmod{13}. \] In a recent preprint, the author showed that these are the only "canonical'' congruences.
  Here, we complete the classification of Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}$, showing that if $\operatorname{spt}(\ell n+b)\equiv0\pmod\ell$ for all $n\geq0$, where $\ell\geq5$ is prime, then $(\ell,b)\in\{(5,4),(7,5),(13,6)\}.$ That is, Andrews' congruences are the only Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

title: On silting theory for complete path algebras
summary: Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $Λ$ be the complete path algebra of $Q$ with respect to the arrow ideal. We study the mutation of silting objects in the bounded homotopy category of projective $Λ$-modules and characterise in which cases the mutation theories of silting complexes and 2-term silting complexes of $Λ$ are determined by those of a finite dimensional quotient $Λ/I$. This characterisation is closely related to a characterisation of 2-term silting finite quotient algebras.

title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
summary: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.

title: Compatible gradings on dg models and cluster equivalence
summary: Let $\La_1$ and $\La_2$ be finite-dimensional $\ta_2$-finite complex algebras of global dimension at most two. We prove that, if they are cluster equivalent, then they admit $\bbZ$-gradings for which the bounded derived categories of graded modules are triangle equivalent. The equivalence is not required to commute with the internal grading shifts. The proof uses common multigraded dg models, relative gradings on two-term silting objects, and covering quotients. We also consider tilting lifts of cluster-tilting objects with endomorphism algebras of global dimension at most two. In acyclic cluster type, the existence of such a lift for every cluster-tilting object implies piecewise heredity. We construct a counterexample without this assumption using a surface algebra associated with a one-holed torus.

title: On integers $n$ relatively prime to $\lfloor αn^2\rfloor$
summary: For $α\in\mathbb{R}$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_{α,k}(x):=\#\{n\in\mathbb N:n\le x,\ \gcd(n,\lfloorαn^k\rfloor)=1\}$. Roth conjectured, and Watson proved, that $S_{α,1}(x)\sim 6x/π^2$ for every irrational $α$. Whether the same asymptotic holds for every fixed $k\ge2$ is a special case of a question of Bergelson and Richter, and was asked explicitly by Champagne. We answer this for $k=2$, with no Diophantine condition on $α$: for every irrational $α$, $S_{α,2}(x)\sim x/ζ(2)$ as $x\to\infty$. More precisely, for every fixed $A>0$ we obtain an error term $O_A(x/(\log q(x))^A)$, where $q(x)$ is the largest continued-fraction convergent denominator of $α$ not exceeding $x$. The proof sieves $S_{α,2}(x)$ over divisors, splitting at the parameter $R=q(x)^{1/8}$. Divisors larger than $R$ are handled by reducing the condition $d\mid\gcd(n,\lfloorαn^2\rfloor)$ to Möbius sums over arithmetic progressions and applying Zhan's uniform estimate for exponential sums twisted by $μ(n)$ over short intervals; divisors at most $R$ are handled instead through the Erdős-Turán inequality together with Weyl-type bounds for quadratic exponential sums of the form $\sum e(βn^2)$.

title: Ramified tori and Gelfand--Kirillov dimension of mod $p$ representations
summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension of degree $n$ with $p\geq3$, and let $D$ be the non-split quaternion algebra over $K$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional admissible smooth representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(K)$ or $D^\times$ with a central character and satisfying a Casimir annihilation condition has Gelfand--Kirillov dimension $n$. As a corollary, every infinite-dimensional admissible Banach representation whose locally analytic vectors have an infinitesimal character has dimension $n$, strengthening Sorgdrager's bound to an equality. An appendix by Yongquan Hu proves that, when $K\ne\mathbb{Q}_p$ and the coefficient field is algebraically closed, the canonical diagram of an admissible supersingular representation satisfying the same Casimir annihilation condition is $(π,π,\mathrm{id})$, as in the case of local fields of characteristic $p$.

title: The smallest-parts function and elliptic curves
summary: Recently, Ono established a new connection between partition congruences and the arithmetic of elliptic curves by expressing the partition function $p(n)$ as a CM trace on the modular curve $X_0(6)$. This approach yields new proofs of Ramanujan-type congruences for the partition function modulo powers of $5$, $7$, and $11$, revealing how the geometry of supersingular elliptic curves and the arithmetic of oriented optimal embeddings govern these congruence properties. Motivated by Ono's work, we develop an analogous passage from CM traces to congruences modulo $5$, $7$, and $13$ for the for Andrews's smallest-parts partition function $spt(n)$, employing the established theta-lift and modular-trace methods suited to this setting. With $P$ the Bruinier--Ono weight-zero weak Maass function and $f$ an explicit weakly holomorphic modular function on $Γ_0(6)$, the Ahlgren--Andersen formula expresses $spt(n)$ as one twelfth of the discriminant $1-24n$ CM trace of $f-P$. We explain the theta-lift normalization, the contribution of the two orientations, and the harmonic-Maass-form uniqueness argument. Following Garvan's work, we construct integral forms $G_\ell$ of weight $\ell+1$ on $Γ_0(\ell)$, compute their Fricke transformations, and prove the exact identities $$ \mathcal T_5(G_5)=-5E_6,\qquad \mathcal T_7(G_7)=-7E_8,\qquad \mathcal T_{13}(G_{13})=13E_{14}. $$ Their reductions yield the three congruences on the Andrews's smallest-parts partition function. We also give a supersingular specialization of the trace of $f$, with actual reduction multiplicities, and explain the role of imprimitive forms, the conductor restriction in CM reduction, and the distinction between the primes $11$ and $13$. These results have been verified in Lean using AxiomProver.

title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
summary: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

title: Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time
summary:
Let $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients of absolute value less than $2^b$. Using Pan's approximate factorization theorem, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds all distinct integer roots of $f$ in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations. This matches the bit size of the input up to logarithmic factors and does not require $f$ to be square-free. Since we were unable to verify parts of the running time analysis of Pan's theorem, we also give a self-contained deterministic algorithm with running time $\widetilde O(nb+\min(n,b)^3b^2)$, which is $\widetilde O(nb)$ whenever $b\leq n^{1/4}$. This answers a question of Harvey and Hittmeir (2022), who asked whether integer roots can be found deterministically in quasilinear time, conditionally on Pan's theorem, and unconditionally for $b\leq n^{1/4}$. The fastest previous deterministic algorithm, due to Nir, takes $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}b)$ bit operations and works only for square-free polynomials.
  Instead of $p$-adic lifting, we combine approximate complex root finding with exact polynomial evaluation. We first approximate the complex roots of the polynomial formed by the top $\min(n,b)+1$ coefficients of $f$. Every integer root $r$ of $f$ with $|r|\geq 2$ lies within distance $2$ of some complex root of this truncated polynomial. Rounding the real parts of the approximate roots therefore gives a list of $O(\min(n,b))$ candidate integers that is guaranteed to contain all integer roots of $f$. Although a single candidate can have up to $b$ bits, a bound via the Mahler measure shows that the bit lengths of all candidates sum to $O(b)$. This allows us to test all candidates by exact multipoint evaluation in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations.

title: The Extension groups of one $\rm K$-type representations of graded Hecke algebra
summary: We study the extension groups between one $\rm K$-type representations of the graded Hecke algebra $\mathbb H$. A one $\rm K$-type representation is a Hermitian representation of $\mbb H$ whose restriction to the Weyl group is irreducible. Using a Koszul-type resolution of $\mathbb H$-modules, we reduce the computation of $\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathbb H}^j(X,Y)$ to a combinatorial count, yielding explicit formulas for the classical types and a computer computation for the exceptional types.

title: Counting irreducible skew polynomials $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$
summary: We give a counting formula for the coefficients $a\in\F_{p^h}$ for which $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{p^h}[x;σ]$, for arbitrary positive integers $n$ and $h$, where $σ(a)=a^p$ and $p$ is an arbitrary prime power. The proof reduces the problem to quadratic reduced norms, establishes a uniformity statement for every Frobenius generator, and counts the remaining coefficients by Möbius inversion.

title: Effective results in representation theory of reductive groups over local fields
summary: We prove effective versions of several classical results in representation theory of reductive groups over non-Archimedean local fields of arbitrary characteristic. More specifically, we deal with the support of matrix coefficients of cuspidal representations and the recursions satisfied by matrix coefficients of representations of finite length. We provide effective generation results for irreducible representations. Finally, we study the effective smoothness of characters on the set of regular semi-simple elements.

title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
summary: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.

title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
comment: 28 pages including 16 pages of a Magma program
summary: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$, the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$ acting on $Λ$, where $L$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ having no real places, the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. We also compute $Sha^S(K,G)$ in some cases where $S$ contains archimedean places.

title: Asymptotics for partitions over the Fibonacci numbers and related sequences, II
summary: In a recent paper of the same title, we considered nondistinct partitions of integers over the Fibonacci sequence and related linearly recurrent sequences. In this paper, continuing this story, we apply the same method, but consider distinct partitions. In particular, let $q_F(m)$ denote the number of ways of writing $m$ as the sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers. It is well-known that, while $q_F(m)$ behaves wildly, its partial sums behave in a more structured way. In particular, Kempton showed that the function $N^{-\log 2/\log\varphi}\sum_{m\leqslant N}q_F(m)$ is asymptotically logarithmically-periodic. In this paper, we improve on this result by providing an explicit error term. Additionally, we prove the analogous result for a class of more general linear recurrent sequences.

title: Derived Ringel duality through finite subquotients of modular category $\mathcal O$
summary: We study derived Ringel duality for modular category $\mathcal O$ on downward-closed, quasi-bounded supports. We reconstruct global tilting objects and their morphisms from compatible images in finite highest-weight Serre subquotients, and realize the complete Ringel algebra as an inverse limit of finite-dimensional algebras. The duality identifies the bounded homotopy category of finitely generated projectives over the associated locally unital algebra with the bounded derived category of the Ringel dual category. We characterize tiltings recovered, together with their outgoing morphisms, by a single finite subquotient, and give a sharp criterion for equivalence under Frobenius restriction. For $SL_2$, we compute tilting endomorphism algebras and their quotient maps, and obtain sharp recovery bounds for finite tilting families.

title: On the Diophantine equation $Cx^2+p_1^{2m_1}p_2^{2m_2}\cdots p_k^{2m_k}=y^q$
summary: Let $C>3$ be an odd square-free integer, $q$ an odd prime not dividing the class number of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-C})$, and $p_1,\dots,p_k$ distinct odd primes not dividing $C$. We describe all solutions of $Cx^2+p_1^{2m_1}\cdots p_k^{2m_k}=y^q$ in positive integers with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y$ odd. Writing $N=p_1^{m_1}\cdots p_k^{m_k}$, every solution comes from a unique factorization $x\sqrt C+N\sqrt{-1}=\pm(u\sqrt C\pm v\sqrt{-1})^q$, or from a half-integral analogue when $q=3$, in which each $p_i\ne q$ divides exactly one of $v$ and $N/v$. Using primitive divisors of Lehmer sequences, we show that for $q\ge5$ some $p_i$ satisfies $p_i\equiv\leg{-C}{p_i}\pmod q$; in particular, there is no solution when $q\ge\max(5,p_1+2,\dots,p_k+2)$. For $q=3$ the equation reduces to four explicit auxiliary equations.

title: On Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers
comment: 147 pages, 4 figures. Preliminary version; comments welcome. TeX and Lean sources at https://github.com/so-okada/kronecker-euler-sources
summary: We prove Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers for each $m \geq 3$ on the normalized logarithms of Euler characteristics of moduli spaces. Also, we state a log-concavity conjecture on Euler characteristics near slope one for the 3-Kronecker quiver.

title: Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(ζ'/ζ)^{k}$
summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(ζ'/ζ\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $Λ^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A unitary trace-sum average governs the variance of sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over monic polynomials in $\mathbb F_q[T]$; we denote its leading coefficient by $δ_k(c)$, where the total trace degree and matrix size grow with a fixed ratio $c$. Under a weaker shifted moments conjecture and RH, we recover this $δ_k(c)$ as the leading coefficient of the variance of short-interval sums of $Λ^{*k}$ over the integers. It is the counterpart of $γ_k(c)$, the piecewise polynomial from the variance of divisor sums, with the Dirichlet coefficients of $ζ(s)^k$ replaced by those of $\bigl(-ζ'/ζ\bigr)^k$.

title: Normality of marginal inverse subsemigroups in inverse semigroups
summary: For each pair of integers $m\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2$, we construct a finite inverse semigroup $S_{m,n}\subseteq M_m(\mathbb{C})$ and explicitly determine its marginal inverse subsemigroup $M_{x^n}(S_{m,n})$ associated with the word $x^n$. We prove that the three conditions $\sim_{x^n}=\equiv_{x^n}$ on $S_{m,n}$, $M_{x^n}(S_{m,n})\trianglelefteq S_{m,n}$, and $m\le n$ are equivalent. As a consequence, we answer Problem 11 of Araújo, Araújo and Kinyon in [1]. Moreover, for a word $ω$ in any inverse semigroup $S$, we prove that $\sim_ω=\equiv_ω$ if and only if $M_ω(S)\trianglelefteq S$ and $\sim_ω$ is invariant under inversion.

title: On partitions with bounded multiplicity restrictions on even parts and with the largest part being odd
summary: Andrews and El Bachraoui (\textit{RACSAM} \textbf{119}, \textit{Article Number 4 (2025)}) established identities relating $4$-regular partitions to partitions with distinct even parts whose largest part is odd. As an extension to their work, in this paper we define partitions of a positive integer $n$ with bounded multiplicity restriction on even parts and whose largest part is odd. We prove some identities relating our partition functions and $2r$-regular partition function, and show that identities due to Andrews and El Bachraoui follow as particular cases.

title: Decompositions of homomorphisms of abelian $p$-groups with $p^2$-bounded target
summary: Let $p$ be a prime. We classify homomorphisms $H:V_1\to V_2$ between abelian $p$-groups that are direct sums of cyclic groups, under the assumption $p^2V_2=0$. We prove that every such homomorphism is isomorphic to a direct sum of finite indecomposable representations and that this decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and reordering of the summands.

title: Divisibility Properties of Odd Part and Even Part Sums in Cubic Partitions
summary: A cubic partition of a positive integer $n$ is a partition of $n$ in which even parts may appear in two distinct colors. The purpose of this paper is to study the arithmetic functions $COS(n)$ and $CES(n)$, which denote the sums of all odd and even parts, respectively, in all cubic partitions of $n$. We obtain their generating functions and divisor-sum formulas, and establish Ramanujan-type congruences modulo $3$, $4$, $5$, and $7$. To prove these congruences, we use Lambert series, classical theta-function identities, dissections, coefficient extraction, and weighted Euler identities.

title: Base change between canonical basis and path basis
summary: Almost 30 years ago Littelmann conjectured that there is a unitriangular base change between the dual canonical basis and the path vector basis for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras. In this paper we give a positive answer to the conjecture for the case of classical Lie algebras and type $G_2$, when the path model is given by standard Young tableaux.

title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
summary: We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.

title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
summary: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.
